report.summary: Chunk 2 of vendors.py: closed vocabularies (STATUSES, LANES, UNAVAILABLE_REASONS), constants, identity helpers (_slug, actor_id, model_family), and VendorReply dataclass start.
risks: PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE | medium | The notice is a prompt injection mitigation that assumes the model will follow it; no code enforces it. | Add runtime enforcement or accept as documented assumption.
model_family | medium | Heuristic may over-merge distinct models, reducing effective independence. | Review over-merge cases and consider explicit mapping.
DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST | low | Hardcoded IP may become stale or unreachable. | Document as example or externalize configuration.
BENCH_SSH_TARGET | low | Hardcoded admin target with IP; security and maintainability concern. | Externalize or document as test-only fixture.

claims.text: Transport outcome of one ``ask``.  CLOSED -- an adapter may not invent a sixth.  None of these is a judgement about the reviewed work; "ok" means the bytes came back, nothing more.
claims.why: STATUSES is defined as a tuple of exactly those 5 strings; no sixth present.

claims.text: Egress lane for a participant.  ``untrusted`` turns the allow-list / default-deny tier ON (``sensitivity.slice_egress_rule``).
claims.why: LANES is defined; the claim about sensitivity.slice_egress_rule refers to another module not present.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- never free prose -- so a council record can be aggregated.
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS is a tuple of fixed string literals, no free prose.

claims.text: Not "localhost": avoids the IPv6 (::1) miss on Windows, same as providers/ollama.py.
claims.why: The constant is defined as http://127.0.0.1:11434; the claim about providers/ollama.py is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Prepended to EVERY outbound prompt.  The evidence under review was written by a candidate model; a diff can carry text addressed to the reviewer and there is no delimiter that makes an LLM reliably treat text as data.  The mitigation is not a better delimiter -- it is that an injection attempt becomes a FINDING.  (The structural mitigation is that nothing here can act.)
claims.why: The constant is defined; claims about prepending to every outbound prompt and structural mitigation refer to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: NO LOCAL-HOST TABLE HERE, ON PURPOSE. "Do the bytes leave this machine" has exactly one implementation, ``sensitivity.lane_for_host``, imported above -- it is the predicate that switches the tier-2 allow-list, so a second copy next to it is a second answer to a safety question.
claims.why: The comment asserts absence of a local-host table; that is true in this chunk. The claim about sensitivity.lane_for_host refers to an external module.

claims.text: Make a model id safe for an actor segment without losing information.
claims.why: Function replaces non-alphanumeric/._- characters with '-', returns 'unknown' for empty/None input; no information loss beyond replacement.

claims.text: ``council.<vendor>.<model>`` per ``docs/adrs/010-naming-namespaces.md``. A bare ``actor: "claude"`` in a durable record is a defect, and it is also not reproducible: the model behind a stable command name changes underneath it, so a dissent attributed only to a vendor cannot be re-run six months on. The FORMAT is delegated to :func:`bus.actor_id` so the id on a transcript turn and the id on the reply that produced it cannot drift apart; this function only normalises the raw model id first (a raw ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` would otherwise put a colon in a durable identifier).
claims.why: actor_id is defined and calls _slug then _bus_actor_id; the claim about delegation and ADR-010 is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Coarse weight family, for :attr:`VendorReply.independence_class`. The unit of independence is WEIGHTS, not endpoints.  Local ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` and bench ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` are one voice on two sockets, and the 1.5b/7b/14b/32b line are near-clones of each other; a council that degrades to "Ollama plus Ollama" reports two participants and holds one opinion.  Heuristic and deliberately coarse -- it strips the tag (``:7b``) and any trailing size/version token, so it OVER-merges rather than under-merges.  Over-merging costs a seat; under-merging silently fakes independence.
claims.why: The function strips tag after ':', removes trailing size/version tokens using regex, and joins remaining parts. The description matches the code.

observations.what: PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE is a long string constant intended to mitigate prompt injection, but there is no enforcement code in this chunk.
model_family heuristic may over-merge models, which could affect independence calculations.
DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST and BENCH_SSH_TARGET are hardcoded IP addresses; may become stale or pose security concerns.
The claim about 'sensitivity.lane_for_host' being the single implementation of local-host detection is uncheckable; if false, could cause security inconsistency.
